checks: The normalized positive central body is eligible for maximal-inscribed-simplex normalization. The transformed volume D lies in [1/d!,2^d], and translating by the simplex centroid then scaling by D^(−1/d) gives the stated outer and inner radii with determinant magnitude one.

The relative-interior point admits strictly positive weights on all of P. Compatibility gives the inclusion of the weighted Minkowski sum, yielding diameters at most 2R/p_z and positive central volume whenever any summand has positive volume.

The affine shear removes translations at an affine basis without changing the central body. The two positive weight perturbations have the same base barycenter and their chosen-point sums differ by 2ε_z c_z. This bounds every nonbasis center even with negative affine coordinates.

The affine map fixes every base, multiplies every fiber measure by one common determinant factor and carries closed halfspaces bijectively, preserving normalized depth. The argument matches a14cc5f809b2b766 §§1–3 including deficient base rank.

dependencies.hypotheses: Its maximal-volume simplex cube normalization applies to the positive-volume central body, without a near-extremal depth hypothesis. The proof uses no rigidity conclusion in this invocation.

overlap.comparison: The accepted one-body maximal-simplex normalization supplies the anchor only. Fixed positive barycentric weights and the common shear extend it to all fibers.
That fixed-projection cap-volume result assumes a minimizer and supplies no uniform affine frame for a minimizing sequence.

readability: The hypotheses and the proof use the same scope.
review_method: Independent cold read of the exact frozen candidate, followed by source, hypothesis, overlap and arithmetic checks.
summary: A single admissible affine normalization controls every fiber diameter and every residual translation over a fixed nonhollow lattice projection.
